goal: Plan AWG V1.9 maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Purpose
V1.9 should make AWG actively resist graph decay. By this point AWG can store rich knowledge, attribute writes to runs, render human-friendly node details, and understand related vault topology. The next highest-value slice is an agent-facing maintenance inbox and append-only reconciliation model so agents can see what needs attention before stale, duplicated, unsupported, or unresolved knowledge becomes invisible.

## Primary Outcome
An agent can run a deterministic inbox command and immediately see the highest-priority maintenance work: stale knowledge, duplicate-ish nodes, orphans, evidence gaps, open questions, active risks/blockers, proposed decisions that may be stale, and cross-vault topology issues. The same data should feed doctor, run preflight, handoff, task lens, and the viewer without adding a daemon, database, network service, or AI dependency.

## Non-Goals
Do not add semantic/vector search, hosted sync, a daemon, MCP, plugin execution, multi-user permissions, arbitrary merge rewriting, or destructive cleanup. V1.9 should not try to solve full role/domain lenses, arbitrary dashboards, claims/evidence verification, or concurrent multi-agent locking. It should build the reliable maintenance substrate those later slices need.

## Definition Of Done
AWG can deterministically say what needs maintenance, why it matters, how severe it is, which nodes/runs/vault relationships are involved, and which conservative commands could repair or review the issue. Reconciliation is append-only: agents can mark duplicates, supersession, contradictions, canonical relationships, and resolutions without deleting or rewriting canonical history.
summary: Build deterministic maintenance queues and append-only reconciliation so agents can keep AWG brains fresh, de-duplicated, evidenced, and reviewable over time.
title: AWG V1.9: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Required Queues
V1.9 should derive a maintenance inbox from compiled graph state, diagnostics, run attribution, freshness metadata, evidence links, and topology indexes. Initial queue kinds should include: stale, needs_review, duplicates, orphans, evidence, questions, risks, blockers, decisions, topology, and hygiene.

## Prioritization
Each item should have deterministic severity and priority. Suggested severity values: info, warning, error. Suggested priority inputs: fatal diagnostics first, completed work missing evidence, active blockers/risks, stale high-importance nodes, duplicate candidates, orphan nodes, unanswered questions, topology warnings, and lower-risk hygiene items.

## Agent Use
The inbox should be small and actionable by default. Agents need item IDs, codes, reasons, involved node IDs/run IDs/vault IDs, suggested commands, and whether the item is safe for autonomous repair or needs human review.
summary: Derive prioritized maintenance queues for stale, duplicate, orphaned, unsupported, unresolved, risky, and topology-related graph issues.
title: V1.9 requirement: deterministic maintenance inbox queues

body:
## Inbox Item Shape
Suggested JSON shape:

```json
{
  "id": "mi:...",
  "kind": "stale|duplicates|orphans|evidence|questions|risks|blockers|decisions|topology|hygiene",
  "code": "AWG_INBOX_STALE_NODE",
  "severity": "info|warning|error",
  "priority": 80,
  "message": "Node is past review_after and still marked current.",
  "nodeIds": ["n:..."],
  "edgeIds": [],
  "runIds": [],
  "vaultIds": [],
  "relationshipIds": [],
  "reasons": ["review_after is in the past"],
  "suggestedCommands": ["awg update node n:... --status needs_review"],
  "autonomousSafe": true,
  "needsHumanReview": false
}
```

IDs should be deterministic from kind/code/targets so repeated builds are stable. Unknown fields should be preserved where events are involved, but compiled inbox items can be derived objects.
summary: Define stable, deterministic JSON for maintenance inbox items so agents can parse and act on graph hygiene work.
title: V1.9 contract: maintenance inbox item JSON

body:
## Reconciliation Principle
V1.9 should not destructively merge or delete graph history. Reconciliation should be represented as durable append-only graph events or nodes/edges that compile into clear current-state relationships.

## Initial Relationships
Support or document these reconciliation relations: duplicate_of, canonical_for, supersedes, superseded_by, contradicts, resolved_by, verified_by, derived_from, and intentionally_open.

## Commands
Recommended CLI surface:
- `awg reconcile duplicate <a> <b> --canonical <id> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile supersede <old> <new> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile contradict <a> <b> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile resolved-by <target> <resolver> [--reason "..."] [--json]`

These commands should append normal events/edges, preserve run attribution, and never mutate old log entries. They should fail clearly for missing targets and avoid cross-vault writes unless an explicit future topology contract allows it.
summary: Represent duplicates, supersession, contradictions, canonical relationships, and resolutions as append-only graph history, not destructive merges.
title: V1.9 contract: append-only reconciliation model

body:
## Commands
Add or improve:
- `awg inbox [--kind <kind>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`
- `awg inbox show <item-id> [--json]` if useful
- `awg reconcile ...` commands for append-only cleanup markers
- `awg doctor --fix-suggestions --json` should share suggestion generation with the inbox where practical

## Integrations
Inbox data should feed: doctor, run finish preflight, handoff, task lens, resume lens if budget allows, and the viewer maintenance surface. Handoff should mention high-priority unresolved inbox items. Run preflight should include inbox items affecting touched nodes. Task lens should include inbox items related to the goal or matching nodes.

## Viewer
Add a minimal read-only maintenance route if it fits the existing viewer architecture: queue filters, item detail, linked nodes, suggested commands, and severity. Do not redesign the viewer.
summary: Expose maintenance inbox and reconciliation through stable CLI/JSON, doctor/preflight/handoff/lens integrations, and a small viewer surface if low-risk.
title: V1.9 contract: inbox CLI and integration surfaces

body:
## Main Risks
- Inbox bloat: too many low-value items makes agents ignore it.
- False duplicate candidates: simple lexical matching can overstate duplicates.
- Unsafe repair suggestions: agents may run commands that mutate too much.
- Reconciliation ambiguity: duplicate/supersede/contradict semantics can become unclear.
- Cross-vault leakage: topology inbox items must not read private/full data beyond the relationship visibility contract.
- Preflight friction: completed runs should be warned strongly, but partial/blocked/failed runs must remain usable.

## Mitigations
Keep defaults compact, deterministic, and conservative. Mark candidate duplicates as review items rather than facts. Suggestions should prefer review/status/evidence/link commands, never destructive commands. Keep reconciliation relations documented and narrow. Keep cross-vault inbox items summary-only unless the relationship explicitly allows more. Add tests for JSON stability and non-mutating dry/read paths.
summary: Maintenance inbox and reconciliation can fail through bloat, false duplicates, unsafe suggestions, ambiguous semantics, cross-vault leakage, or excessive preflight friction.
title: V1.9 risk register: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Required Test Areas
- Inbox derivation for stale nodes, needs_review nodes, orphans, evidence gaps, unanswered questions, active risks/blockers, proposed decisions, duplicate candidates, doctor diagnostics, and topology issues.
- Stable JSON item shape with deterministic IDs, severity, priority, target IDs, suggested commands, and autonomous/human review flags.
- `awg inbox --json`, kind filtering, limits, empty vault behavior, and parseable output.
- Reconciliation commands append events/edges with run attribution, preserve unknown fields, fail clearly for missing targets, and do not mutate old events.
- Doctor fix suggestions and inbox suggestions stay aligned and non-mutating.
- Run finish preflight includes relevant inbox items for touched nodes without blocking partial/blocked/failed runs too aggressively.
- Handoff and task lens include compact unresolved maintenance context within budget.
- Viewer maintenance route does not crash on missing/old inbox data.
- Old vaults without reconciliation events still compile.
- Tests isolate HOME/temp dirs and do not touch real ~/.awg.
summary: Test derived inbox queues, stable JSON, reconciliation commands, doctor/preflight/handoff/lens integrations, viewer compatibility, and old-vault behavior.
title: V1.9 test plan: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Suggested Slices
1. Inspect current diagnostics, preflight, handoff, task lens, freshness, duplicate-ish diagnostics, topology diagnostics, and viewer data generation.
2. Create a core maintenance inbox derivation module that consumes compiled graph state and emits stable inbox items.
3. Add `awg inbox` CLI with `--json`, `--kind`, and budget/limit behavior.
4. Share conservative suggestion helpers between inbox and doctor where practical.
5. Add append-only reconciliation commands and compiler interpretation of reconciliation relations.
6. Integrate relevant inbox items into run preflight, handoff, task lens, and resume/current view if low-risk.
7. Add a minimal read-only viewer maintenance route if it fits without redesign.
8. Update docs, generated instructions, examples, and tests.
9. Run adversarial/peer review loops after each meaningful slice: 1 reviewer for low-risk docs or CLI polish, 2 reviewers for core inbox/reconciliation logic, and 3 reviewers only for final release readiness or cross-cutting behavior.
summary: Implement V1.9 in slices: derive inbox items, expose CLI, share suggestions, add reconciliation, integrate surfaces, update viewer/docs/tests, and use bounded reviewer loops.
title: V1.9 implementation sequence and review loop

body:
The user priority after V1.9 is: V2.0 view primitives / human operating surfaces, V2.2 claims-evidence-verification, V2.3 agent work queues, and V2.4 multi-agent coordination. Role/domain lenses remain useful but should not become a fixed hard-coded domain pack release. When AWG revisits lenses, agents should be encouraged to define, review, and iterate vault-local lens configurations similar to operating templates, so lenses adapt to the actual domain and project rather than forcing universal categories.

This means V1.9 should avoid overfitting to role lenses. It should expose generic maintenance inbox data and stable primitives that future configurable lenses can consume.
summary: After V1.9, prioritize view primitives, claims/evidence verification, work queues, and multi-agent coordination; defer role/domain lenses until they can be vault-configured by agents like templates.
title: Roadmap decision: prioritize maintenance substrate before configurable lenses

body:
## Purpose
This roadmap captures enough durable direction for AWG V2 planning without over-specifying future slices before V1.9 is fully evaluated. The strongest near-term sequence is V2.0 view primitives, V2.2 claims/evidence verification, V2.3 agent work queues, and V2.4 multi-agent coordination. V2.1 configurable lenses and V2.5 long-term scale/archival remain useful but lower priority.

## Planning Rule
Each future slice should start by reading this roadmap plus the latest maintenance inbox, dogfood feedback, V1.9 results, and any active operating template. Do not implement from roadmap summaries alone; create an implementation-grade spec when that version becomes the active target.
summary: Durable summary of likely AWG V2.0-V2.5 directions, with V2.0, V2.2, V2.3, and V2.4 prioritized over configurable lenses and archival scale work.
title: AWG V2 roadmap summary

body:
## Goal
Give humans a glanceable operating surface that is materially better than Markdown walls or raw graph lists. Agents should be able to populate safe, structured view primitives that the viewer renders consistently.

## Candidate Primitives
Tables, checklists, timelines, metric rows, status boards, relationship maps, evidence lists, task queues, run summaries, comparison matrices, and current-effort dashboards.

## Constraints
Use deterministic structured data, not arbitrary HTML or executable agent-authored rendering. Preserve tokenized viewer styling. Keep the first slice small and compatible with existing blocks/viewer architecture. This should be the foundation for human confidence in what agents are doing right now.
summary: Expand safe structured presentation primitives so agents can create glanceable human surfaces for current work, evidence, queues, timelines, metrics, and relationships.
title: AWG V2.0: view primitives and human operating surfaces

body:
## Goal
Make lenses configurable by vault agents rather than shipping rigid role/domain lenses. This remains lower priority than V2.0, V2.2, V2.3, and V2.4, but it is the right direction when AWG returns to role/domain entry points.

## Model
Lens configs should resemble operating templates: durable graph knowledge with selector rules, included node types, queue kinds, status filters, budget priorities, output sections, and review metadata. Agents may propose and iterate them, but changes should be visible and reviewable.

## Constraint
Avoid hard-coded domain packs as the main strategy. Built-in defaults can exist, but vault-local lens configuration should be the long-term adaptation mechanism.
summary: Let agents define and refine vault-local lens configurations like templates, instead of hard-coding role/domain lenses as the main adaptation strategy.
title: AWG V2.1: configurable vault lenses

body:
## Goal
Separate what AWG knows from what AWG merely believes. Long-lived brains need first-class support for claims, assumptions, verification status, source reliability, contradictions, evidence expiry, and current-vs-historical truth.

## Candidate Capabilities
Claim nodes or claim fields, `verified_at`, `verification_status`, evidence expiry/review dates, source reliability, contradicted_by relationships, confidence history, and commands such as `awg add claim` or `awg verify <node>` if they fit the codebase.

## Why It Matters
This is critical for research, SEO, trading, business operations, and software docs where stale or unsupported claims can silently become harmful.
summary: Add stronger claim and verification semantics so AWG can distinguish current facts, assumptions, historical facts, contradicted claims, and evidence-backed knowledge.
title: AWG V2.2: claims, evidence, and verification

body:
## Goal
Turn AWG from memory plus maintenance into an agent operating queue. Agents should know what work is safe to do next, what requires human approval, what is blocked, what needs evidence, and what maintenance should be handled now.

## Candidate Queues
`next`, `autonomous`, `human_review`, `blocked`, `evidence_needed`, `maintenance`, `stale_review`, `risk_review`, and `handoff_followup`.

## Dependency
Build on V1.9 maintenance inbox rather than inventing separate queue logic. V2.3 should promote selected inbox items, tasks, risks, and run follow-ups into prioritized work queues.
summary: Create deterministic work queues so agents can select next actions, autonomous-safe work, human-review items, blocked work, evidence gaps, and maintenance follow-ups.
title: AWG V2.3: agent work queues

body:
## Goal
Support many agents working in one vault or related vaults without stepping on each other. Coordination should remain local-first and append-only, not real-time multi-user infrastructure.

## Candidate Capabilities
Task claiming, run ownership, active-work warnings, touched-node conflict warnings, per-run open items, cross-run collision diagnostics, stale claims, handoff-to-agent conventions, and queue-aware assignment.

## Constraint
Do not add hosted collaboration, daemon sync, or heavyweight locking. Start with warnings and durable claims that agents can inspect and honor.

body:
## Problem
When AWG gains new capabilities, agents may keep using older workflows unless the human explains the change. That creates adoption drag and makes new features less valuable.

## Desired Behavior
Each release should expose deterministic, local release notes for agents. On startup, handoff, resume, or instruction install/upgrade, agents should be able to see what changed, what new commands are available, and whether the current vault has recommended migrations or optional adoption steps.

## V1.9.1 Scope
Add a local release-notes surface and agent instruction pointer. Prefer a concise file or compiled artifact plus CLI read path such as , , or . Generated AGENTS guidance should point agents to it without bloating AGENTS.md with every release. Release notes should include date/version, highlights, agent actions, migration/adoption suggestions, and links to docs/nodes where useful.

## Deferred Packaging Scope
A true  command belongs later, once distribution through npm or another stable install channel exists. Until then, focus on local awareness and upgrade notes rather than package self-update.

## Constraints
Keep this local-first and deterministic. Do not add hosted sync, network checks, daemon behavior, or auto-mutation of vaults without explicit commands. Agents may suggest adoption or run safe diagnostics, but should not silently rewrite project knowledge just because a feature exists.
summary: AWG should publish concise agent-facing release notes so agents immediately learn new features, migration opportunities, and changed operating guidance after an update.

goal: Plan agent discernment guidance for AWG capture versus chat

body:
## Intent
AWG should be the place agents store durable project knowledge outside transient chat threads. Agents should not wait for the human to explicitly say save this when the user has clearly made a decision, accepted a plan, set a requirement, defined a constraint, identified a risk, assigned work, or provided reusable context.

## Balance
The instruction must avoid two failures. Over-capture turns AWG into a noisy transcript of brainstorming and half-formed thoughts. Under-capture leaves important plans and decisions trapped in chat where future agents cannot retrieve or maintain them.

## Capture Signals
Agents should capture or update AWG when the user confirms direction, chooses an option, asks to proceed, assigns implementation work, states a durable preference, defines a rule, gives a reusable fact, accepts a spec, reports feedback that should affect roadmap or behavior, or changes how a project/domain/process should work.

## Wait Signals
Agents should usually avoid durable writes when the user is only brainstorming, asking hypotheticals, venting, comparing rough options, exploring unclear ideas, or explicitly asking to think without changing the durable record. In those cases, the agent may wait, summarize back, or ask before capturing if the content seems important but unsettled.

## Domain Adaptation
Different vaults can use different capture thresholds. A research or strategy vault may capture open questions and promising hypotheses more liberally. A production codebase or client operations vault should be stricter about only recording confirmed decisions, requirements, active risks, evidence, and implementation-relevant context. Vault operating templates should be able to tune this threshold.

## Agent Behavior
Agents should search before writing, update canonical nodes instead of duplicating, prefer concise summaries plus richer body only when useful, and add run notes for meaningful capture decisions. If the agent is unsure whether a chat idea is durable, it should either wait for a clearer signal or capture it as a question/proposed item with status needs_review rather than as accepted truth.

## Instruction Surface
Generated AGENTS guidance should include a compact rule: do not leave durable knowledge only in chat, but do not mirror the whole conversation into AWG. Capture decisions, requirements, accepted plans, reusable context, risks, evidence, and meaningful feedback once they become actionable or likely to matter to future agents.

## V1.9.1 Scope
Add refined agent instruction wording and examples for capture versus wait behavior. Link this to quick capture and release notes so agents can use low-ceremony commands when the content is worth preserving. Do not add AI classification, semantic search, daemon behavior, or automatic transcript ingestion.

## Later Scope
V2.3 work queues can surface needs_review captured ideas for human review. V2.1 configurable vault lenses/templates can tune capture thresholds by domain.
summary: Agents should automatically persist durable knowledge to AWG, but distinguish exploratory conversation from decisions, requirements, plans, commitments, and reusable context that belong outside the chat thread.

body:
## Core Rule
Do not leave durable work knowledge trapped only in chat, and do not mirror chat into AWG. Capture or update AWG when the information is likely to help a future agent understand, continue, verify, maintain, or safely change the work.

## Future-Agent Test
Capture when at least one is true:
- It changes future behavior, requirements, scope, priorities, acceptance criteria, or constraints.
- It records a decision, accepted plan, active task, risk, blocker, evidence, source-of-truth boundary, or stable project preference.
- A future agent would likely search for it before continuing the work.
- Losing it would create rework, ambiguity, safety risk, client risk, stale context, or source-of-truth confusion.

## Capture Signals
Capture or update AWG when the user confirms a direction, chooses an option, approves work, rejects an approach, corrects the agent, states a durable preference, defines a rule or boundary, identifies a risk, assigns work, accepts a spec, changes roadmap priority, provides reusable project/domain context, or gives feedback that should change future behavior.

Do not treat a routine phrase like "go ahead" as durable by itself. Capture it only when it confirms a specific plan, requirement, decision, or commitment that future agents need.

## Wait Signals
Usually do not write durable AWG records for brainstorming, hypotheticals, rough comparisons, venting, reactions, compliments, routine status updates, command-by-command narration, discarded options, or unclear ideas. If exploratory discussion produces a likely future input, preserve it as tentative rather than asking the user to babysit capture.

Create a needs_review question, proposal, or hypothesis only when there is a clear future review target and losing the item would create real project risk or rework. Otherwise leave unsettled ideas in chat.

## Truth And Status
If content is not confirmed, do not store it as accepted truth. Use the right shape: question, hypothesis, proposal, needs_review, low confidence, risk, blocker, task, evidence, or decision. Research and strategy vaults may preserve more tentative items, but they must be labeled as tentative. Production, client, financial, or operational vaults should default stricter.

## Ask Threshold
Agents should normally capture useful internal, reversible, clearly labeled context silently. Ask before capturing only when the user explicitly requested think-only mode, the capture would assert unsettled content as approved truth, it conflicts with current source-of-truth knowledge, it includes sensitive information, or it would imply external publication, client-facing action, trading action, financial commitment, or source-of-truth mutation.

## Minimal Payload
Capture the consequence, not the conversation. Prefer "Decision: use X for Y because Z" over recording who said what, how the discussion unfolded, or every option considered. Search before writing, update canonical nodes instead of duplicating, and create the smallest useful durable unit. Batch related minor facts into an existing node or run note instead of creating many tiny nodes.

Do not add run notes just to narrate routine capture or non-capture. Reserve run notes for material progress, blockers, evidence, force-finish rationale, or capture decisions that future agents must understand.

## Evidence
Evidence is proof behind a claim, not all logs or all chat. Examples include test output, source citation, client approval, analytics snapshot, meeting decision, backtest result, policy reference, command result, or before/after verification. Attach evidence when work is completed, claims need support, or future agents need verification context.

## Domain Examples
- Code: capture accepted architecture, constraints, test evidence, risks, source-of-truth boundaries, and implementation plans; do not capture every debug log or transient hypothesis.
- Research: capture source-backed findings, labeled hypotheses, open questions, contradictions, and rejected paths with rationale; do not capture raw reading notes unless synthesized.
- Content/blog: capture approved strategy, briefs, voice rules, keyword decisions, source maps, internal-linking rules, and publish constraints; do not capture every draft sentence.
- Business operations: capture process decisions, owner changes, recurring workflows, KPIs, risks, approvals, and high-priority contact rules; do not capture routine chatter.
- Trading/research ops: capture thesis, assumptions, risk rules, datasets, backtest evidence, invalidation criteria, and market-event research; do not capture live trade instructions unless the vault policy explicitly allows it.
- Client work: capture client preferences, approvals, scope changes, blockers, evidence, and delivery decisions; redact sensitive details and do not replace the CRM, contract, billing system, or approval record.

## Template Tuning
Vault operating templates may tune capture strictness: strict, balanced, or exploratory. They should be able to define preferred node types, default statuses for unsettled items, required fields by node type, evidence standards, freshness/review cadence, sensitive-data and redaction rules, external source-of-truth boundaries, and lens priorities for tasks, decisions, risks, evidence, questions, and stale context.

## Instruction Surface
Generated AGENTS guidance should include compact wording like:

Use AWG for durable project knowledge, not transcript storage. Search first, then update the canonical node or create the smallest useful node. Capture decisions, requirements, accepted plans, reusable constraints, risks, blockers, tasks, evidence, source-of-truth boundaries, and actionable feedback once they affect future work. During brainstorming, wait or capture only as needs_review/question/hypothesis. Follow the vault template for stricter or more exploratory capture thresholds.

## V1.9.1 Scope
Add refined agent instruction wording and examples for capture versus wait behavior. Link this to quick capture and release notes so agents can use low-ceremony commands when content is worth preserving. Do not add AI classification, semantic search, daemon behavior, automatic transcript ingestion, or external-memory sync.

## Later Scope
V2.3 work queues can surface needs_review captured ideas for human review. V2.1 configurable vault lenses/templates can tune capture thresholds by domain.
